claims.claim: Second-quarter revenue was $17.2 billion, up 1% year-over-year.
Gross profit was $9.9 billion, down 1% year-over-year.
Pre-tax income was $2.5 billion, down 5% year-over-year.
Net income was $2.2 billion, down 2% year-over-year.
claims.note: Release's income statement summary shows net income of $2.2B down 1% year/year; the (2) percent decline belongs to GAAP diluted EPS ($2.27 vs $2.31), not net income.

claims.claim: Software revenue was $7.8 billion, up 5% year-over-year.
Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) was up 11% in the second quarter.
Data was up 19% in the second quarter.
Automation was up 4% in the second quarter.
Consulting revenue was $5.3 billion, flat year-over-year.
Both Strategy and Technology and Intelligent Operations were up 1% at constant currency.
Infrastructure revenue was $3.8 billion, down 7% year-over-year.
The Infrastructure decline was driven by a 42% decline in IBM Z.
The IBM Z decline was partially offset by a 37% increase in Distributed Infrastructure.
The company expects full-year constant currency revenue growth in the range of 4% to 5%.
IBM anticipates free cash flow to increase by about $1 billion year-over-year for the full year.
Second-quarter free cash flow was $2.5 billion, down $0.3 billion year-over-year.
Total debt, including IBM Financing debt, was $62.0 billion, up $0.7 billion year-to-date.
The company expects currency to be neutral to growth for the full year.
